To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the B → (K,K ∗ )l+l− decay rates and the FB-asymmet- ries are in general sensitive to new flavor violating interactions in the SM and SUSY models and that the present experimental upper limit on B(B → K∗µ + µ − ) and the existing measurements of FB-asymmetry and B(B → Xsγ) provide interesting constraints on the underlying new physics.

the present data on B → (K, K ∗ ) µ + µ − decays, in conjunction with B → Xs γ, already provide interesting constraints on new physics, that the FB-asymmety in B → K l + l − decays is a precision test of both the SM and its possible extensions and that future experiments may reveal new phenomena.
the FB-asymmetric in B → K l + l − can be used to distinguish among different SUSY models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What is the present status of B → (K,K ∗ )l+l− in the SM?
the following questions: (1) How well can we predict the decay rates and the dilepton mass spectrum in the SM and in SUSY theories?

the following issues: (i) Theoretical precision on B → (K,K ∗ ) l + l − in the SM and SUSY models; (ii) The role of the form factors in B → K and K ∗ transitions; (iii) Bounds on the Wilson coefficients of the effective theory; (iv) FB-asymmetry as a precision test of SM; and (v) FB-asymmeties in the SUSY models as a probe of new physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SM predictions for the B → Xs γ, B → (K,K ∗ )l l and FB-asymmetriies in B → K l l are consistent with the data and the existing theoretical uncertainties.
the present experimental results on the B → K l + l − and B → K ∙ l + l − decay rates and FB asymmetry are consistent with the SM predictions, but do not exclude the possibility of a new physics.
the FB-asymmetric in the decays $B \rightarrow (K, K^{*})\ell^{+} \ell^{-}$ is a very promising tool for testing the SM and for revealing the presence of physics beyond the SM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decays B→ (K, K*)l+l− are very promising in the search of new physics beyond the SM.
the decays B→(K,K∗)l+l− can be used to probe the underlying physics of flavor violation in the SM and in many of the popular variants of SUSY theories.
the B → (K,K ∗ )l ± l ± decays provide an interesting window for the exploration of the physics beyond the SM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B → (K,K ∗ )l l decays provide a powerful testing ground for the SM and its possible extensions.
the FB-asymmtery in B → K l + l − can be used to discriminate among various models of new physics.
the B → K l + l − decays provide an interesting window to search for physics beyond the SM.
